correctness.rationale: For finite interior atoms, ℓ_i(t)=t log a_i+(1−t)log(1−a_i) has increasing slopes and only consecutive upper-envelope crossings c_i. The Bayesian binomial posterior therefore concentrates on the unique maximizing atom; near a crossing the triangular-array binomial CLT yields the Gaussian Φ interface, with weights contributing only O(1) trial shift. Reversible positive semidefinite finite-site Markov matrix has off-diagonals controlled above by pairwise binomial-overlap sums, and at a minimizing adjacent crossing has a matching lower term. Stirling + two geometric tails yield Θ(n^(−1/2)exp(−nC_*)); trace and Rayleigh bounds yield the operator norm. Fixed atoms, weights, and site count are crucial; no exact constant is asserted.
